To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the kinetics of the coloration of a-WO3 is controlled by a diffusion process of an intermediate species into the oxide.

the kinetics of the coloration of amorphic tungsten oxide films (a-W03) is controlled by the diffusion of an intermediate species M+ (Li+, H+) into the oxide, and by the rate of the redox reaction between this species and a W6+ (WO3) ion.
the kinetics of the coloration of amorhous tungsten trioxde is slower than the electrochemical reaction, and that the coloration kinetics is controlled by the diffusion of Li+ and H+ in the oxide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the kinetics of color change and with the modelling of this phenomenon in a-WOx.
the kinetics of colorations of a-WO3 films and with the determination of the molar absorption coefficients of LixWO3 (x<1) and HxWO 3 (x<2).
the kinetics of the coloration and bleaching of a-WO3 thin films.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kinetics of the coloration of a-WO3 in acid or lithium electrolytes is controlled by a diffusion of a redox intermediate species into the oxide.
the coloration of a-WO3 is controlled by the kinetics of the diffusion of the electroactive ions (Li+ and H+) into the oxide.
the electrochromic properties of a-WO3 depend on the nature of the electrolyte and on the nature of its ions.
